analyst_view.overall: Sparta Prague (22nd, 4 pts) host AZ (14th, 6 pts) at Letna in turmoil: Brian Priske was sacked on Monday after a 3-1 home defeat to Liberec, and Lukas Blaza, coach of third-tier partner club Loko Praha, leads the team as interim coach, saying he will keep Priske's principles. Sparta have won one of their last nine, lost their last three home games by two goals, and only about 7,000 tickets had been sold, so Letna may see its lowest European crowd in years. Defender Tobias Guddal is banned after a red card (not counted); Karabec and Rynes are back in training but not ready (counted), Kofod Andersen, Penxa and Uchenna are out and Eneme and Sochurek doubtful. AZ, who beat Sparta 2-1 and 4-0 in March, have won their last two with nine goals but miss Smit, Patati, Schouten, Resink and Hornkamp (mostly counted). Portuguese referee Antonio Nobre is in charge, and both sides play again in their leagues three days later.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (AZ 1.6) and know nothing of the coach being sacked three days before kick-off or of Guddal's ban, which weakens Sparta's back line. A low-confidence side under a stand-in coach against an AZ attack that has scored nine in two points to a slightly more open game, so I go to about 3.1; a possible reaction from the players keeps it small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, mostly AZ (5.7), already up a little for Sparta conceding many corners lately. Blaza expects a well-structured, pressing AZ side and wants to keep Priske's possession game rather than sit deep, so the upheaval does not obviously change the corner count and I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already raised for Sparta's recent bookings (15 in six) and trimmed for referee Antonio Nobre's short, calm record. Macek, Singhateh and Suchomel are one booking from a ban and tension around the club could add a card, but a half-empty stadium and Guddal's absence point the other way, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.7 shots, already up about 12% for AZ's busy recent shooting (100 in six). Sparta's turmoil could tilt the game further toward AZ, but the numbers already have AZ well ahead on shots and AZ are missing Smit and Patati, so I stay at 26.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. With Sparta's back line short of Guddal (not counted) and the team in disarray after the sacking, AZ should get a few cleaner chances, so I go slightly higher, to about 9.1.
